metadata.purpose: The prior context ("make sure to") makes the intended word unambiguous; later layers fold that context into the misspelled token's vector, pushing it toward the correct token's direction, and the Jacobian lens traces the shift layer by layer.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to understand what the Jacobian lens shows about how a model processes a misspelled token. Ask Claude to walk you through what the output-to-input Jacobian tells you for a single token — and why a model can know the correct spelling in its middle layers even when the input carries the typo.

props.command: I want to use the Jacobian lens to understand how a language model processes a misspelled token in the input. Walk me through what the Jacobian of the output with respect to a single input token tells you — and show me why a model can 'know' the correct spelling in its middle layers even when the input carries a typo.
